title: Finite-support coherent modules decompose into finite-length skyscrapers
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose $S=\{x\in X:F_x\ne0\}$ is a finite set of closed points. Write $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $M_x=F_x$ for $x\in S$. Each $M_x$ is a nonzero finite $A_x$-module whose localization at every prime of $A_x$ other than its maximal ideal is zero, and it has finite length: there are $r\ge1$ and $A_x$-submodules
$$0=M_0\subsetneq M_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq M_r=M_x$$
whose successive quotients are nonzero and have no proper nonzero submodule. Define $\mathscr S_x(M_x)$ to be the ringed module skyscraper [def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper], with sections $M_x$ on opens containing $x$ and zero otherwise, restrictions the identity whenever both opens contain $x$, and scalar action through the germ $\mathcal O_X(U)\to A_x$. The morphisms sending a section to its germ at each $x\in S$ assemble into a canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
$$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{x\in S}\mathscr S_x(M_x).$$
At a point $y\in S$ its stalk map is the identity of $M_y$ under the canonical stalk identifications; outside $S$ it is the map $0\to0$. If $S$ is empty this says $F=0$.

proof.text: Fix $x\in S$. Choose an affine open $U\ni x$ from the Noetherian affine covering in [pqf-def-locnoeth], put $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be the prime representing $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the germ map identifies $A_x$ with the local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Since $R$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $A_x$ Noetherian.

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], $F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-stalk-finite] therefore hold and give that $M_x=F_x$ is finite over $A_x$. It is nonzero because $x\in S$. Put $N=F(U)$. By [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization], for every point $z\in U$ corresponding to a prime $\mathfrak r\subset R$, the actual germ map identifies $F_z$ with $N_{\mathfrak r}$; in particular $M_x=N_{\mathfrak p}$, compatibly with the ring germ map of step 1.

proof.text: Steps 1--3 meet every hypothesis of [lem-sc-generic-stalk-finite-length]: $A_x$ is Noetherian local, $M_x$ is finite and nonzero, and its support is contained in the maximal ideal. Hence $M_x$ has positive finite length. To obtain exactly the filtration in the statement, use the bounded strict-chain definition in [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. The nonempty set of lengths of chains from $0$ to $M_x$ is bounded in $\mathbf N$, so choose a chain of greatest length $r$. Since $M_x\ne0$, $r\ge1$. Any proper nonzero submodule of $M_i/M_{i-1}$ would have an inverse image strictly between $M_{i-1}$ and $M_i$, lengthening this chain. Each successive quotient is therefore nonzero and simple.

Write $T_x=\mathscr S_x(M_x)$ as in [def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper]. The finite product sheaf $T$ has $T(U)=\prod_{x\in S}T_x(U)$: compatible sections glue uniquely in each coordinate, so this is a sheaf. The coordinate inclusions and projections identify it with the finite direct sum: for maps $f_x:T_x\to H$, the map out is $(t_x)\mapsto\sum_x f_x(t_x)$, and its uniqueness follows by writing each tuple as the sum of its coordinate tuples. Define $\eta_U:F(U)\to T(U)$ by the germ $s_x$ in coordinate $x$ if $x\in U$, and zero otherwise. By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], germs commute with restriction and satisfy $(as)_x=a_xs_x$. Therefore $\eta$ is a canonical morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: Definition 009A (definition-skyscraper-sheaf), case (4); Lemma 009C (lemma-stalk-skyscraper-adjoint), explicit germ map

proof.text: For $y\in S$, the open set $V=X\setminus(S\setminus\{y\})$ contains $y$, because all the finitely many excluded points are closed. Every neighbourhood of $y$ can be intersected with $V$, and on every resulting neighbourhood $W$ one has $T(W)=M_y$, with identity restriction maps. By the germ description in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], evaluation of the $y$-coordinate identifies $T_y$ with $M_y$: every germ is represented there, equal coordinates give equal germs on the intersection, and any $m\in M_y$ is represented by the corresponding section on $V$. In these coordinates $\eta_y$ sends $s_y$ to $s_y$, hence is the identity. If $y\notin S$, the open neighbourhood $X\setminus S$ has $T(W)=0$ on all its subopens, so $T_y=0$; by definition of $S$, also $F_y=0$. This proves all the claimed stalk identifications without invoking a commutation of stalks with an infinite product.

source.place: Tag 009B (lemma-skyscraper-stalks); direct neighbourhood calculation for finite closed support

proof.text: Every stalk map of $\eta$ is bijective by step 6. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] to conclude $F\xrightarrow{\sim}T=\bigoplus_{x\in S}\mathscr S_x(M_x)$. For $S=\varnothing$, step 5 defines $T$ to be the zero module sheaf and step 6 still gives bijectivity $0\to0$ at every point, so the same criterion gives $F=0$.

Step 2: coherent-ft-locnoeth, then finite-type stalk finiteness (the same finite-type notion as pqf-def-coherent), then affine-module-germ-localization, which needs quasi-coherence only. Step 3: spectrum-embedding gives q⊊p; a point of S would be closed, forcing q maximal, so F_y=0 and N_q=0. I checked the explicit fraction maps (N_p)_Q↔N_q by hand: well-definedness uses the same cross-multiplied expression killed by uw∉q. Step 4: generic-stalk-finite-length (00L5) gives finite length; a maximal chain under the bounded-chain definition has simple quotients. Steps 5-6 are elementary: finite product and coproduct, germ map, η O-linear by (as)_x=a_x s_x, stalks computed through the opens X∖(S∖{y}) and X∖S. Step 7: module-iso-on-stalks; S empty gives F=0.
